answer: One workable design: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because lagoon only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. In practice nebula is enforced by the ledger itself: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any inlet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
